correctness.rationale: Exact source update gives B_minus=B_plus^T for the sign-reversing bilinear game. On each singular mode, the positive-definite Hermitian period block has trace 2[(1-rho)^2+rho^2]+t^2, determinant (1-2rho)^2+(1-rho)^2t^2>0, and det(I-Q)=-rho(2-rho)t^2<0; therefore exactly one eigenvalue exceeds one. Every nonzero synchronized mode has Rayleigh quotient 1+t^2/2>1, ensuring an expanding projection; nonzero off-diagonal coupling ensures its primary projection is nonzero. Orthogonal SVD modes preclude cancellations. The exact frozen example and 240 numerical eigenvalue tests plus exact sympy identities executed from the bundled verifier; finite checks are not taken as universal proof.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison against Zheng et al. arXiv:2403.09090v1 (DGDA update, static bilinear Theorem 2 and its spectral appendix), Feng et al. arXiv:2310.02604 (time-varying OGDA/NM Theorem 3.2 and Appendix C), and Fiez et al. arXiv:2111.03377 (continuous-time periodic GDA) found no statement covering the new all-rho DGDA Floquet spectrum and divergence from every synchronized nonzero primary initialization. The qualitative possibility of periodic instability is known and excluded from the novel claim. In particular, rho=1/2 DGDA reduces algebraically to OGDA with half the stepsize; that special-case phenomenon is not itself claimed novel.

value.rationale: Directly addresses robustness of a published dissipative saddle-point optimizer under periodic games: the all-parameter structural instability and exact growth spectrum prove that no positive damping in the algorithmic range or arbitrarily small positive step suffices to transfer the static convergence guarantee. Exact every-synchronized-start growth and a stable-frozen but divergent-period example give a useful caution for minmax algorithm and switched-system analysis. This is not merely a routine renaming or a generic high-level time-variation warning; the proof identifies the transposed-period Gram mechanism and sharp mode-by-mode multipliers. The finite-dimensional sign-reversal model and auxiliary initialization limits are explicit.
